Problem: Let \( n \in \mathbf{Z}_{+} \). When \( n > 100 \), the first two digits of the decimal part of \( \sqrt{n^{2}+3n+1} \) are ______.

<reflection>
We are given n ∈ Z₊ and n > 100. We need the first two digits of the decimal part of √(n² + 3n + 1).
The equality is false because (n + 1)² − 2n = n² + 1, not n² + 3n + 1.
Correct the algebra: use a true rewriting such as n² + 3n + 1 = (n + 1)² + n, then apply a valid square-root approximation.
</reflection>
